newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Monetarist Czech PM meets Keynesian Nobel laureate.
newsitem.headline: Monetarist Czech PM meets Keynesian Nobel laureate.

text.p: Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Monday met Nobel Prize-winning economist James Tobin to discuss problems in the Czech and American economies, a government spokesman said.

"Vaclav Klaus and James Tobin spoke about problems in the transformation of the Czech economy, about privatisation and exchange rates and actual problems of the American economy," Klaus's spokesman Ivo Strejcek said in a statement.

The meeting brought together two rather different views -- Klaus, a professor of economics and an unabashed monetarist, and Tobin, the Yale professor and 1981 Nobel laureate for his work on Keynesian demand-side economic theories.
Neither was available for further comment after the meeting.
Tobin is most remembered for his proposal of the so-called "Tobin Tax" on foreign exchange transactions, a measure aimed at helping to limit economic volatility caused by global currency flows.
The proposal has been roundly rejected by monetarist economists and is said to be unworkable by many politicians.
